text: Call any LLM provider through one unified completion() interface without learning provider-specific APIs
quote: Call any provider using the same completion() interface, with no API to re-learn for each one

text: Swap providers without rewriting code via drop-in OpenAI-compatible interface
quote: Drop-in OpenAI compatibility — swap providers without rewriting your code

text: Normalizes every provider's response into the OpenAI Chat Completions format
quote: Every response follows the OpenAI Chat Completions format, regardless of provider.

text: Load-balance requests across multiple deployments (e.g. Azure/OpenAI)
quote: Load-balance across multiple deployments (e.g. Azure/OpenAI)

text: Automatically fails over to a healthy backup model/provider after retries are exhausted
quote: If a call fails after num_retries, LiteLLM falls back to another model group, so a failing model or provider automatically fails over to a healthy backup.

text: Self-hosted LLM gateway/proxy you can run yourself
quote: Self-hosted LLM Gateway (Proxy) with virtual keys, cost tracking, and an admin UI

text: Tracks spend for keys, users, and teams across 100+ LLMs in one place
quote: Track spend for keys, users, and teams across 100+ LLMs.

text: Create personal virtual keys with individual spending limits
quote: Personal budgets: Create virtual keys without team_id for individual spending limits

text: Track spend and control which models a key can access via virtual keys
quote: Track Spend, and control model access via virtual keys for the proxy

text: Gateway-level caching of LLM responses to cut cost and latency on repeat requests
quote: LiteLLM's caching system stores and reuses LLM responses to save costs and reduce latency.

text: Log proxy input, output, and exceptions to observability tools like Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, GCS, S3, Azure Blob
quote: Log Proxy input, output, and exceptions using: Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, GCS, s3, Azure (Blob) Buckets...

text: Generates a unique call_id per request for tracing it across the system
quote: LiteLLM generates a unique call_id for each request. This call_id can be used to track the request across the system.

text: Can disable logging of message/response content while still tracking spend metadata
quote: This will prevent the messages and responses from being logged to your logging provider, but request metadata - e.g. spend, will still be tracked.

text: Configurable number of worker processes (uvicorn, gunicorn, or Granian) for the proxy
quote: The number of worker processes to spin up (uvicorn, gunicorn, or Granian --workers).

text: Provides an MCP Gateway exposing a fixed endpoint for all MCP tools with access control by Key/Team
quote: LiteLLM Proxy provides an MCP Gateway that allows you to use a fixed endpoint for all MCP tools and control MCP access by Key, Team.

text: Put entire AI stack behind one key to see who drives spend and cap it before it runs, routing each request to the right model
quote: Put your full AI stack behind one key. See who is driving spend, cap it before it runs, and send each request to the model that should handle it.

text: Consistent output format across providers and models
quote: Consistent output format regardless of which provider or model you use

text: Maps content policy violation errors consistently across providers for content policy fallbacks
quote: content_policy_fallbacks: For litellm.ContentPolicyViolationError - LiteLLM maps content policy violation errors across providers

text: On failure, proxy loops through configured fallback model groups until one succeeds
quote: The request to `model="zephyr-beta"` will fail... litellm proxy will loop through all the model_groups specified in `fallbacks=["gpt-3.5-turbo"]`

text: Tag requests to track spend by tag
quote: pass tags to track spend by tags

text: Apply budgets across all proxy calls with configurable reset frequency (e.g. 30 days)
quote: Apply a budget across all calls on the proxy... budget_duration: 30d # (str) frequency of reset

text: Set rate limits (e.g. requests-per-minute) per team via team configuration
quote: "team_alias": "my-new-team_4", ... "rpm_limit": 99

text: Add and manage MCP servers directly from the LiteLLM admin UI
quote: On the LiteLLM UI, Navigate to "MCP Servers" and click "Add New MCP Server".
